title: Create blog-posts.ts data file with TypeScript types and slug generation utility
description: Establish a centralized, type-safe blog post data source using TypeScript. Define BlogPost interface with title, slug, author, publishDate, description, category, content, and featuredImage. Implement slug generation utility that converts titles to deterministic URL-safe slugs.
acceptanceCriteria: BlogPost interface exported from site/src/data/blog-posts.ts with required fields: title, slug, author, publishDate, description, category, content, featuredImage
slug utility function (site/src/lib/slug-utils.ts) generates consistent URL-safe slugs (e.g., 'Getting Around JB' → 'getting-around-jb') with no duplicate slugs
At least 6 blog posts defined with backpacker/traveler content theme (JB, Singapore, visa, jobs, transport)
technicalNotes: File to create: site/src/data/blog-posts.ts (export const blogPosts: BlogPost[] with BlogPost interface definition)
File to create: site/src/lib/slug-utils.ts (export function generateSlug(title: string): string using toLowerCase + kebab-case)
Test command: npx tsc --noEmit to verify types; grep -c 'slug:' site/src/data/blog-posts.ts should equal post count

title: Add Article JSON-LD schema to blog post layout with author, publishDate, image, and wordCount
description: Implement Article schema.org structured data for blog posts. Extract metadata from blog post data (title, author, publishDate, description, featuredImage, wordCount) and generate valid JSON-LD embedded in the page head that Google Search Console recognizes for rich result display.
acceptanceCriteria: Article JSON-LD schema in blog post layout (site/src/app/blog/[slug]/layout.tsx) includes @context, @type, headline, author, datePublished, image, description, and wordCount fields
Schema validates successfully using Google's Rich Results Test with no errors; passes JSON-LD syntax validation
Schema <script> tag has id='article-schema' for test verification and is placed before closing </head>
technicalNotes: File to edit: site/src/app/blog/[slug]/layout.tsx - add generateMetadata export that returns structured data in metadata.other
File to create: site/src/lib/blog-schema.ts (export function generateArticleSchema(post: BlogPost, wordCount: number): object)
Test command: curl -s http://localhost:3000/blog/[post-slug] | grep -o '"@type":"Article"' should return match; validate with: npm install --save-dev @types/schema.org

title: Generate RSS/Atom feed at /feed.xml using next-rss with auto-discovery link in layout
description: Create an RSS 2.0 feed endpoint that exports the 10 most recent blog posts with title, description, author, pubDate, and link. Add auto-discovery link tag to the layout head so RSS readers and search engines can discover the feed automatically.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /feed.xml returns valid RSS 2.0 XML with <rss version='2.0'>, <channel>, and <item> elements, sorted by pubDate descending (newest first)
Each <item> contains <title>, <description>, <author>, <pubDate (RFC 822 format)>, <link>, and <guid> matching post slug URL
Layout head includes <link rel='alternate' type='application/rss+xml' href='/feed.xml' title='Pelangi Blog Feed' /> in site/src/app/layout.tsx
technicalNotes: File to create: site/src/app/feed.xml/route.ts (export async function GET() { return new Response(rssString, { headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/xml' } }) })
Install rss package: npm install rss, or build RSS string manually with template literals and XML encoding
Test command: curl -s http://localhost:3000/feed.xml | head -20 should show valid XML; npx rss-parser 'http://localhost:3000/feed.xml' should parse without errors

title: Create /blog index page with category filter, post listing, and responsive grid layout
description: Build the main blog landing page that displays all blog posts in a responsive grid. Implement client-side category filtering with toggle buttons and render blog post cards with title, excerpt, author, publishDate, and featured image. Ensure mobile-first responsive layout.
acceptanceCriteria: Page route site/src/app/blog/page.tsx renders all posts from blogPosts data, sorted by publishDate descending; displays post count
Category filter buttons toggle visibility (e.g., selecting 'Backpacking' shows only posts with category: 'backpacking'), 'All' shows all posts; active filter state visually highlighted
Blog post cards display title, excerpt (first 150 chars), author, publishDate, featured image; responsive grid: 1 col mobile (<640px), 2 cols tablet (640-1024px), 3 cols desktop (>1024px)
technicalNotes: File to create: site/src/app/blog/page.tsx - use 'use client' for state, useState for selectedCategory filter, import blogPosts from site/src/data/blog-posts.ts
File to create/edit: site/src/components/BlogCard.tsx - display post preview card with Image, title, excerpt, author, date; use responsive image sizes
Test command: npm run dev && curl -s http://localhost:3000/blog | grep -c '<article' should match post count; filter by category in browser dev tools Network tab

title: Build JB News & Updates widget for homepage fetching from 3 curated travel news RSS feeds
description: Create a reusable widget component that fetches the latest 3-5 news items from curated RSS feeds (e.g., JB tourism, travel blogs, local news). Display items as a card list on the homepage with title, snippet, and link. Include loading and error states for robustness.
acceptanceCriteria: Widget component site/src/components/JBNewsWidget.tsx fetches from 3 hardcoded RSS feed URLs (define in site/src/lib/rss-utils.ts) using async fetch; displays 3-5 most recent items
Each item renders with title (linkified to original), description (first 100 chars), source name, and pubDate; shows loading spinner while fetching, error message if fetch fails
Widget renders on homepage (site/src/app/page.tsx) in a scrollable or card-grid layout; data refetches on each page load (no stale cache)
technicalNotes: File to create: site/src/components/JBNewsWidget.tsx - use 'use client', useState, useEffect; import parseRSSFeed from rss-utils; handle loading/error states
File to create: site/src/lib/rss-utils.ts (export const RSS_FEEDS: string[] = [...], export async function parseRSSFeed(url: string): Promise<NewsItem[]>) using xml2js or rss-parser
Test command: npm run dev && visit http://localhost:3000, open Network tab, filter by 'feed' or 'rss'; check widget displays 3-5 items within 5 seconds; npm install xml2js or rss-parser
